message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe – has a range of distinctive physical, chemical, and nuclear properties:

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Standard atomic weight** | ~1.008 u (average of isotopes) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (¹H, no neutrons), Deuterium (²H, one neutron), Tritium (³H, two neutrons; radioactive) |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14 K) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) |
| **Density at STP** | 0.0899 g/L (≈0.0000899 kg/m³) |
| **Molar mass** | 1.00794 g/mol (protium) |
| **Ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (first ionization) |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (negative, meaning it releases energy when gaining an electron) |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **Oxidation states** | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride ion H⁻) |
| **Bond dissociation energy (H–H)** | 436 kJ/mol (104 kcal/mol) |
| **Heat capacity (Cp)** | 29.12 J/(mol·K) at 298 K |
| **Specific heat (Cp)** | 14.304 J/(g·K) at 298 K |
| **Thermal conductivity** | 0.180 W/(m·K) at 300 K |
| **Electrical conductivity** | Very low as a gas; becomes metallic under extreme pressure (~400 GPa) |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; reacts with oxygen to form water vapor (exothermic). |
| **Reactivity** | Forms hydrides with metals (e.g., NaH, CaH₂), acids (forming H₂ gas), and many organic compounds (alkanes, alcohols, etc.). |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR) – key in astrophysics. |
| **Nuclear properties** | Lightest element; used in fusion research (D‑T fusion). |

### Key Chemical Behaviors

- **Diatomic nature**: Exists naturally as H₂ molecules (except for the rare monatomic H atoms in high‑energy environments).
- **Acidity**: In aqueous solution, H₂O ⇌ H⁺ + OH⁻; the proton (H⁺) is the basis of acid–base chemistry.
- **Redox reactions**: Acts as both reducing agent (e.g., H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O) and oxidizing agent (e.g., H₂O₂ → H₂O + ½ O₂).
- **Hydride formation**: Forms ionic hydrides with electropositive metals (NaH, MgH₂) and covalent hydrides with nonmetals (CH₄, NH₃).

These properties make hydrogen central to fields ranging from combustion engines and fuel cells to astrophysics and nuclear fusion research.
